document_title: Over $19 million for a Lubbock computing cluster, and the announcement gives no install date
_note: Slide strings read off each frame's own HTML.
caption:
Lubbock has a computing cluster on paper.

In January the Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund gave Texas Tech $12 million toward a clean room. The university will match it for a $24 million project. In May a Texas Tech engineering team received roughly $4.5 million for wide and ultrawide bandgap semiconductor research. On November 13th Texas Tech announced another award of over $19 million to help set up a computing cluster in Lubbock.

The project will combine AI with simulation data and lab results. Engineering dean Roland Faller says Texas Tech will be one of the first universities with access to the newest generation of Nvidia chips to power the cluster.

The cluster is not built yet. The announcement gives no install or completion date.

The deck draws each award as wafers, one for every $1 million.

When does Texas Tech put a date on it?

S2.headline: Lubbock, by way of the governor's office
S2.body: The Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund is administered by the Texas CHIPS Office in the Office of the Governor. The Texas CHIPS Act created it in 2023. The new cluster is to stand in Lubbock.

S3.headline: January brought $12 million for a clean room
S3.body: The fund gave Texas Tech $12 million in January toward a clean room for semiconductor work. Twelve wafers, capped at both ends, drawn to illustrate.

S4.headline: Texas Tech will match it, for a $24 million project
S4.body: The university will match the state's funding, bringing the clean room project to $24 million. The state's twelve wafers sit in a quartz boat and Texas Tech's twelve in a dark carbide boat. Drawn to illustrate.

S5.headline: May added roughly $4.5 million
S5.body: In May a Texas Tech engineering team received roughly $4.5 million from the fund for wide and ultrawide bandgap semiconductor research. Four wafers and a cleaved half, drawn to illustrate.

S6.headline: Three awards, three kinds of number
S6.body: January was a stated $12 million. May was roughly $4.5 million. November is over $19 million, which is a floor. No total is drawn.

S7.headline: AI to steer how the crystals grow
S7.body: The project will integrate AI with high-fidelity simulation data and experimental results, which the university says should shorten development cycles. Planned work includes AI-enabled epitaxial growth of ultrawide-bandgap semiconductors. Drawn to illustrate.

S8.headline: The newest Nvidia chips, the dean says
S8.body: The engineering dean, Roland Faller, says Texas Tech will be one of the first universities with access to the newest generation of Nvidia chips to power the cluster. The university describes a cluster as servers working as one system. Drawn to illustrate.

S9.headline: No install date announced
S9.body: Texas Tech's November 13th announcement says the award will help establish the cluster. It gives no install or completion date. The plate is drawn to illustrate.
